DAMGHANI:v1p450/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p450/r3.anchor: النداء الأمر قوله سبحانه في سورة الشعراء

STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r5.claim: The first narrative recounts Moses' confrontation with Pharaoh, the sorcerers, and the Israelites' flight from Egypt.
STUDYQURAN:26:intro/r5.anchor: partial telling of the account of Moses’ confrontation with Pharaoh, his duel with the sorcerers, and the flight from Egypt

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r1.claim: This section expands the Moses and Pharaoh account from the command to confront Pharaoh through the drowning of Pharaoh and his army.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r1.anchor: This anecdote begins at the instant when Moses (sws) and Aaron (sws) were asked to go to the Pharaoh and ends on the destruction through drowning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r2.claim: The account's episodes reassure the Prophet and his companions and instruct his opponents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r2.anchor: Each and every part of this anecdote is a source of assurance to the Prophet (sws) and his companions and teaches a lesson to his rivals.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r3.claim: People enslaved by desire remain unmoved even by great miracles and awaken only when they see their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p404/r3.anchor: those who lose their ability to understand by becoming slaves to their desires are not influenced by the greatest of miracles

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r1.claim: The passage recalls God's call to Moses on his return from Midian in the sacred valley of Tuwa, where he was appointed and sent to Pharaoh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r1.anchor: while he was returning from Madyan, God spoke to him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā. He was assigned messengerhood

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.claim: The question about fearing God portrays Pharaoh and his people as extremely rebellious; the author paraphrases it as an uncontrolled rise in injustice without fear of God's wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r2.anchor: Will these unjust people continue to increase in their rebelliousness in an uncontrolled manner and not fear God’s wrath?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.claim: This warning style conveys anger, yearning, rebuke, and the nearness of God's punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r3.anchor: Anger, yearning, rebuke and the proximity of God’s scourge found in this style does not need any elaboration.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.claim: The author says other prophets warn their peoples in the same way later in this sūra.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p407/r4.anchor: It will become evident from verses 125, 143, 162 and 178 ahead that other prophets too warned their nations in this way.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r11.claim: After Quraysh rejected revelation, Moses' story consoles the Prophet; Quraysh worshipped other gods, while Pharaoh's people treated Pharaoh as a god, and Moses' followers lived beside Muhammad's believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r11.anchor: ولما ذكر تكذيب قريش بما جاءهم من الحق وإعراضهم عنه، ذكر قصة موسى عليه السلام، وما قاسى مع فرعون وقومه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r12.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies an implicit command to recite the story as the governing element of إذ, citing Abraham's story as a parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r12.anchor: والعامل في إذ، قال الزجاج، اتل مضمرة، أي اتل هذه القصة فيما يتلو إذ نادى، ودليل ذلك واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم إذ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r13.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r13.claim: Another analysis makes اذكر, “remember,” the governing verb for إذ, equivalent here to recite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r13.anchor: وقيل: العامل اذكر، وهو مثل واتل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r14.speaker: وقيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r14.claim: نادى may mean “called,” or, in another gloss, “commanded.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r15.claim: The أن introducing the command may be a masdariyya particle or an explanatory particle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p141/r15.anchor: وأن: يجوز أن تكون مصدرية، وأن تكون تفسيرية،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r1.claim: The narrative begins with an implied command to remember when God called Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r1.anchor: التقدير واذكر إذ نادى ربك موسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r3.claim: The particle an before the command may be explanatory with no syntactic position, like ay, or accusative by supplying bi-an before the command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p226/r3.anchor: وقوله أن ائت يجوز في أن أن تكون مفسرة لا موضع لها من الإعراب بمنزلة أي

JISHUMI:v7p5342/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r12.claim: Nidāʾ is a summons in the vocative form, as if God first called O Moses and then gave the command.
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r12.anchor: النداء: الدعاء على طريقة يا فلان، فكأنه تعالى نادى بأن قال: يا موسى، ثم أمره.

JISHUMI:v7p5342/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r16.claim: Qawm is accusative after iʾti, either as an appositive to the first qawm or as an explanatory accusative.
JISHUMI:v7p5342/r16.anchor: نصب (قوم) ب (ائت) وهو بدل من القوم الأول، وقيل: نصب على التفسير.

RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r1.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r1.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī says Moses heard God’s eternal speech, which is audible yet unlike letters and sounds, just as God Himself is unlike created things.
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r1.anchor: فقال أبو الحسن الأشعري : المسموع هو الكلام القديم

RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r2.speaker: أبو منصور الماتريدي
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r2.claim: Abū Manṣūr al-Māturīdī says Moses heard a call made of letters and sounds: vision supports a common cause of existence across visible things, but hearing supplies no parallel proof that every existent thing is audible.
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو منصور الماتريدي : الذي سمعه موسى عليه السلام كان نداء من جنس الحروف والأصوات

RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites agree that the heard call consisted of letters and sounds.
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r3.anchor: أما المعتزلة فقد اتفقوا على أن ذلك المسموع ما كان إلا حروفا وأصواتا

RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites say the call was miraculous because Moses knew it came from God and was addressed to him; no intermediary was needed. At the start of prophethood he was to summon people to monotheism, then receive legal commands, knowing miracles would appear if demanded.
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r4.anchor: فعند هذا قالوا إن ذلك النداء وقع على وجه علم به موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r5.claim: The people are called wrongdoers both because their disbelief wrongs themselves and because they wrong the Israelites.
RAZI-FULL:v24p105#2/r5.anchor: من وجه ظلمهم أنفسهم بكفرهم ، ومن وجه ظلمهم لبني إسرائيل

BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r1.claim: The temporal clause is governed by an implied “remember.”
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r1.anchor: إذ منصوب باذكر المقدر والمناداة والنداء رفع الصوت

BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r2.claim: Munādāt means raising the voice; the root evokes moisture, associated with eloquence because a moist mouth produces beautiful speech.
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r2.anchor: والمناداة والنداء رفع الصوت وأصله من الندى وهو الرطوبة واستعارته للصوت

BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r3.claim: Muḥammad is told to recall for his people God’s call to Moses by the burning tree when he returned from Midian, and to warn them of Pharaoh’s people’s fate.
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى اذكر يا محمد لقومك وقت نداءه تعالى وكلامه موسى أي ليلة رأى الشجرة والنار حين رجع من مدين

BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r4.claim: The clause beginning an is explanatory after “called,” meaning “that is,” and ītiyān means coming easily.
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r4.anchor: تفسير نادى فإن مفسرة بمعنى أي والإتيان مجيء بسهولة.

BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r5.claim: The people wronged themselves through disbelief and sins, enslaved the Israelites, and slaughtered their sons.
BURSEVI:v6p192#2/r5.anchor: أنفسهم بالكفر والمعاصي واستعباد بني إسرائيل وذبح أبنائهم.

STUDYQURAN:26:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:10/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:10/r1.claim: The fuller account has Moses see a distant fire on the mountain, approach it, speak with God, and receive the mission to go to Pharaoh.
STUDYQURAN:26:10/r1.anchor: Moses’ initial call is mentioned in greater detail in 20:9–48 and 28:29–35

TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.claim: The second “people” specifies the first: the wicked people are Pharaoh’s disbelieving people, and the question asks whether they will fear God’s punishment for disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v17p552/r1.anchor: يعني الكافرين قوم فرعون، ونصب القوم الثاني ترجمة عن القوم الأول

TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.claim: The sequence of earlier prophets shows that Muhammad's people follow the same path and will face punishment; repeated story endings echo the opening rejection, console the Prophet, show his mission is not unprecedented, and implicitly warn his people.
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r1.anchor: ليظهر أن قوم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سائرون مسيرهم وسيردون موردهم

TABATABAI:26:10-13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r2.claim: The verse asks the Prophet to recall when God called Moses and sent him to Pharaoh's people to rescue the Children of Israel, as detailed in Surat Taha and elsewhere.
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r2.anchor: أي واذكر وقتا نادى فيه ربك موسى وبعثه بالرسالة إلى قوم فرعون

TABATABAI:26:10-13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r3.claim: The command explains the call; describing them first as wrongdoers and then as Pharaoh's people points to their shirk and their abuse of the Israelites as the reason for the mission.
TABATABAI:26:10-13/r3.anchor: وتوصيفهم أولا بالظالمين ثم بيانه ثانيا بقوم فرعون للإشارة إلى حكمة الإرسال

TABRISI:26:10-12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:26:10-12/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses “when” as an accusative dependent on an omitted command to recount the story, supported by the following instruction to tell Abraham’s story.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: موضع إذ نصب على معنى واتل عليهم هذه القصة فيما تتلو

TABRISI:26:10-12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r8.claim: The command to go to the unjust people is the object of “called,” as the message Moses was called to deliver.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r8.anchor: موضعه نصب بأنه مفعول نادى أي ناداه بهذه الكلمة

TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.claim: The stories of earlier messengers console Muhammad and urge him to persevere, trusting that victory will come.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r14.anchor: ثم ذكر سبحانه أقاصيص رسله تسلية للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وتحريضا له على الصبر ثقة بنزول النصر

TABRISI:26:10-12/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:10-12/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:10-12/r15.claim: God tells Muhammad to recount the time the Creator called Moses and ordered him to go to people who sinned against themselves and oppressed Israel with severe punishment.
TABRISI:26:10-12/r15.anchor: أي واذكر يا محمد واتل عليهم الوقت الذي نادى فيه ربك الذي خلقك

THALABI:v7p159#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p159#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p159#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to recall when God called Moses upon seeing the tree and fire and ordered him to go to Pharaoh's people.
THALABI:v7p159#2/r1.anchor: وإذ نادى واذكر يا محمد إذ نادى ربك موسى حين رأى الشجرة والنار

THALABI:v7p159#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p159#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p159#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh's people wronged themselves through unbelief and sin, and wronged the Israelites by enslaving them and subjecting them to severe torment.
THALABI:v7p159#2/r2.anchor: القوم الظالمين لأنفسهم بالكفر والمعصية ولبني إسرائيل باستعبادهم وسومهم سوء العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#2/r1.claim: Idh is accusative with an implied command to recount this story; the following command to recount Abraham's story supplies evidence.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r1.claim: The call is to address someone with yā so-and-so; God called Moses after he saw the tree and fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r1.anchor: ومعنى النداء: الدعاء ب: يا فلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r3.claim: They wronged themselves through disbelief and sin, and wronged Israelites by imposing grievous torment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r3.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: يعني الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بالكفر والمعصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r4.claim: The passage next identifies them as Pharaoh's people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p25#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثم أخبر عنهم فقال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to recall when God called Moses on the night Moses saw the tree and the fire.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r1.anchor: { و } اذكر يا محمد { إذ نادى ربك موسى } ليلة رأى الشجرة والنار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:10-11/r2.claim: The people are wrongdoers against themselves through disbelief.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.claim: God commands Moses to go to the wrongdoers, Pharaoh’s people, and calls them to fear God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p496/r3.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإذ نادى ربك موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين {10} قوم فرعون ألا يتقون {11} } [الشعراء: 10-11] ، أي: فليتقوا الله. قال موسى.

QASHANI:26:10-12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:10-12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:10-12/r1.claim: The wrongdoers are tyrannical psychic powers serving the Pharaoh-like commanding soul, which claims lordship and substitutes its own perfection for God's; this is the worst injustice.
QASHANI:26:10-12/r1.anchor: { إن ائت القوم الظالمين } من القوى النفسانية الفرعونية العانية لفرعون النفس الأمارة، المتخذة لها ربا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.claim: Moses faced a harder mission than Muhammad: he came from an enslaved people to summon Pharaoh, while Muhammad shared his audience’s status and faced less powerful opponents; Moses’s success encourages the Prophet and believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:10/r1.anchor: Bu âyetler, o zor şartlarda Hz. Mûsâ nasıl başarılı olduysa Hz. Peygamber’in de öyle başarılı olacağına işaret etmekte, müminlere ümit ve cesaret vermektedir

SULAMI:v2p71#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p71#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p71#5/r1.claim: God secretly summoned Moses to call the people to divine oneness after showing him God's uniqueness, greatness, encompassing knowledge, and power over His servants; Moses then feared they would deny him.
SULAMI:v2p71#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : أسره بدعائهم إلى توحيده وقد أشهده عظمته في انفراده ، وإحاطة علمه ، وقدرته بعباده

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r6.claim: A fourth sense is a command: God’s call to Moses directs him to go to the wrongdoing people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p592/r6.anchor: والرابع : الأمر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء :

SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r1.claim: The governing verb for iḏ is implicit: al-Zajjāj estimates “recite,” while others estimate “remember.”
SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r1.anchor: العام فيه مضمر. فقدره الزجاج: اتل، وغيره: اذكر

SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r2.claim: An can be explanatory or a masdariyya particle, equivalent here to “that you come.”
SAMIN-DURR:26:10/r2.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مفسرة، وأن تكون مصدرية أي بأن

ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r1.claim: إذ is accusative, governed by an understood command to recount this story as part of what is being recited.

ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r2.claim: The later command واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم confirms that this passage is to be recited as a story.
ZAJJAJ:v4p84/r2.anchor: ودليل ذلك قوله عطفا على هذه القصة: (واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.claim: Samarrai observes that every sura beginning with ṭā gives a detailed account of Moses near its beginning, unlike other suras opened by disconnected letters.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r6.anchor: كل سورة تبدأ بالطاء ترد فيه قصة موسى في أوائلها مفصلة قبل سائر القصص

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r1.claim: Al-Aʿraf embeds Moses and Pharaoh in a wider history of the Children of Israel, while al-Shuʿara recounts their story in detail through Pharaoh's drowning; the latter is one part of the former's broader account.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r1.anchor: إن موضوع القصة في سورة الأعراف هو تاريخ من بني إسرائيل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r2.claim: The al-Shuʿara narrative is built around detailed event-by-event telling and strong confrontation; al-Aʿraf is concise and lacks the same force of challenge.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r2.anchor: إن القصة في سورة الشعراء تتسم بسمتين بارزتين هما

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r3.claim: Al-Aʿraf opens with Moses' short message to Pharaoh; al-Shuʿara begins earlier, with God's commission, Moses' fears and request for Aaron, and God's reassurance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r16/r3.anchor: أما في الشعراء فقد بدأت بالأحداث السابقة لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r1.claim: The Moses narrative resumes to confirm the disbelievers' bad state and console the Prophet through another example; إذ is an accusative object and the story is joined to the preceding narrative.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r1.anchor: مستأنف مقرر لسوء حالهم ومسل له صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا لكن بنوع آخر من أنواع التسلية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r2.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r2.claim: One proposed command is to remember privately Moses' rejection despite clear signs, so the Prophet knows earlier nations also denied messengers and can be reassured.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r2.anchor: والتقدير عند بعض واذكر في نفسك وقت ندائه تعالى أخاك موسى عليه السلام وما جرى له مع قومه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r3.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r3.claim: Shaykh al-Islam reads the command as asking the Prophet to remind his people of Pharaoh's punishment, warning them against persistent denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r3.anchor: وعند شيخ الاسلام واذكر لقومك وقت ندائه تعالى موسى عليه السلام وذكرهم بما جرى على قوم فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r4.claim: The author prefers remembering the event for the Prophet's people because 26:69 explicitly says to recount the story to them; he rejects a required private address for stories beginning كذبت.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r4.anchor: والأظهر عندي تقدير وأذكر لقومك لوضوح اقتضاء ( وأتل عليه ) له ولا نسلم اقتضاء تلك القصص

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r5.claim: The story consoles because neither the Prophet nor his people are unprecedented: messengers before him faced rejection despite manifest signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r5.anchor: ليس بدعا من الرسل ولا قومه بدعا من الأقوام في التكذيب مع ظهور الآيات وسطوع المعجزات

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r6.claim: Adding an omitted command such as take the signs or await reports before remember is needless; making إذ a time adverb for a later قال is also rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك المقدر معطوف على مقدر ءاخر أي خذ الآيات أو ترقب اتيان الأنباء واذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r7.claim: نادى means دعا, called or summoned.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r7.anchor: ومعنى نادى دعا وقيل : أمرأمر ( أن ائت

ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r8.claim: أن can be an infinitival particle after an omitted preposition, or an explanatory particle introducing the command ائت.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p63#2/r8.anchor: أي بأن ائت على أن مصدرية حذف عنها حرف الجر أو أي ائت على أنها مفسرة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r1.claim: The people are called wrongdoers for disbelief and sins, enslaving the Israelites, and killing their sons.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r1.anchor: بالكفر والمعاصي واستبعاد بني اسرائيل وذبح أبنائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r2.claim: This is not the opening of God's call to Moses: the fuller call appears in 20:12–23; the Qur'an retells one story in varied wording to suit each context.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p64/r2.anchor: ما فصل في سورة طه من قوله تعالى إني أنا ربك إلى قوله سبحانه لنريك من ءاياتنا الكبرى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r13.claim: Muhammad is told to remember when God called Moses after he saw the tree and fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r13.anchor: واذكر يا محمد إذ نادى ربك موسى حين رأى الشجرة والنار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r14.claim: The wrongdoers sinned through disbelief and disobedience and oppressed the Israelites by enslaving and tormenting them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p107/r14.anchor: {أن ائت القوم الظالمين} يعني: الذين ظلموا أنفسهم بالكفر والمعصية، وظلموا بني إسرائيل باستعبادهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r4.claim: The phrase has an understood “remember,” or is a temporal adjunct governing what follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r4.anchor: مقدر باذكر أو ظرف لما بعده.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r5.claim: أن may substitute for the command ائت, or the command may be governed by an omitted preposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r5.anchor: أن ائت } أي { ائت } أو بأن { ائت }.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r6.claim: Their wrongdoing consisted of unbelief, enslaving the Israelites, and killing their sons.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:8-11/r6.anchor: بالكفر واستعباد بني إسرائيل. وذبح أولادهم.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r6.claim: The narrative exemplifies the preceding ending of al-Furqān: God’s power to seize those ungrateful for blessings and resistant to messengers, while consoling Muhammad through earlier prophetic trials.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r7.claim: The accounts are presented as true history that nearby People of the Book could not deny, proving that the Qur’an is from the Lord of the worlds, not soothsaying or poetry, despite widespread unbelief.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r7.anchor: فصح قطعا أن هذا الكتاب جلي الأمر , على القدر , ليس بكهانة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r11.claim: Moses and Abraham offer the fullest consolation because of their closeness to Muhammad and shared migration and journey toward the Holy Land; Moses is placed first.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r11.anchor: وكانت التسلية بموسى وإبراهيم عليهما السلام أتم , لما لهما من القرب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r12.claim: Moses especially parallels this community through his unmatched scripture and signs, his people’s guidance and preservation, later prophets and conquests, and Israel’s proximity to the Arabs in Medina.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r12.anchor: بالكتاب الذي ما بعد القرآن مثله والآيات التي ما أتى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r13.claim: Because Jews lived nearby and could confirm the account or be asked about it, the story’s public familiarity would make their acknowledgment a powerful proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r13.anchor: مع مجاورتهم للعرب حتى في دار الهجرة , وموطن النصرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r14.claim: As warning, the clause can mean remember God’s long merciful delay for Muhammad’s people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r14.anchor: اذكر أثر رحمتنا بطول إمهالنا لقومك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r15.claim: On the warning reading, the audience is treated as having seen Moses’ call because Jews were nearby: they knew the story or could ask them about it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p348#2/r15.anchor: لأن اليهود في بلادهم وفي حد القرب منهم

DURR-FULL:v6p290/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p290/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p290/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses was called when he was at the right side of the Mount.
DURR-FULL:v6p290/r1.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه {وإذ نادى ربك موسى} قال: حين نودي من جانب الطور الأيمن

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Moses was called from the right side of Mount Sinai.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r1.anchor: السدي واذ نادى ربك موسى قال : حين نودي من جانب الطور

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the wrongdoers as disbelievers.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2751#3/r2.anchor: الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس الظالمين يقول : الكافرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.claim: The passage begins examples confirming the Messenger through the fates of peoples who denied their messengers, warning the audience and recalling arguments delivered by earlier messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r1.anchor: شروع في عد آيات على صدق الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بذكر عواقب المكذبين برسلهم ليحذر المخاطبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.claim: Several famous punishment histories are recounted rather than just one: recurrence weakens the possibility that a people's fate was accidental, since analogical evidence gains certainty through repetition and corroboration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r2.anchor: لأن الدلالة غير العقلية يتطرقها احتمال عدم الملازمة بأن يكون ما أصاب قوما من أولئك على وجه الصدفة والاتفاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.claim: Moses precedes Abraham out of the usual chronological order because the surah answers demands for supernatural signs: Pharaoh's defiance despite Moses' signs exemplifies the disbelievers' resistance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r3.anchor: لعله لأن السورة نزلت للرد على المشركين في إلحاحهم على إظهار آيات من خوارق العادات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.claim: إذ is a time noun governed by an omitted اذكر, as in the later instruction واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم; it also reminds and consoles the Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r4.anchor: اسم زمان منصوبا بفعل محذوف تقديره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.claim: God's calling Moses means revelation through speech Moses heard directly, without an angel intermediary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r5.anchor: ونداء الله موسى الوحي إليه بكلام سمعه من غير واسطة ملك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r6.claim: أن ائت is an explanatory clause clarifying what the call conveyed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r6.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية . والمقصود من سوق هذه القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r7.claim: The admonition's main point is the deniers' eventual fate at the sea; the preceding verses explain Moses' mission, Pharaoh's rejection, and what led to that ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p102#2/r7.anchor: وذلك عند قوله تعالى : { فأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117#4/r1.claim: The implied command is: recite this story to your people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p117#4/r1.anchor: المعنى واتل هذه القصة على قومك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137/r1.claim: God called and spoke privately with Moses from the right side of the mountain, selected him, and commanded him to go to Pharaoh and his people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p137/r1.anchor: حين ناداه من جانب الطور الأيمن، وكلمه وناجاه، وأرسله واصطفاه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r1.claim: Calling them “the wrongdoing people” before specifying “Pharaoh's people” marks them as unjust; the two labels are appositional restatements with the same referent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r1.anchor: سجل عليهم بالظلم بأن قدم الظالمين ، ثم عطفهم عليهم عطف البيان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r2.claim: They deserve the label for wronging themselves through unbelief and evil, and for enslaving the Children of Israel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p307/r2.anchor: وقد استحقوا هذا الاسم من جهتين : من جهة ظلمهم أنفسهم بالكفر وشرارتهم

MUQATIL:26:10-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r1.claim: “When your Lord called” means when God commanded Moses; the address is to Muhammad.
MUQATIL:26:10-15/r1.anchor: يقول: وإذ أمر ربك يا محمد { موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r1.claim: Idh is the object of an implied verb: “remember when.”

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r2.claim: Nāda means that the Lord called Moses.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r3.claim: An here means ay, introducing the content “that is: go.”

NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r4.claim: They wronged themselves through disbelief and the Israelites through enslavement and killing their sons.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p180#6/r4.anchor: أنفسهم بالكفر وبنى إسرائيل بالاستعباد وذبح الأولاد سجل عليهم بالظلم

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r1.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r1.claim: The opening إذ is accusative, with an implied “recite to them,” supported by the following command to recount Abraham’s story.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإذ نادى ربك موسى } { إذ } في موضع نصب المعنى: واتل عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r2.claim: Another construal is “remember when,” as in other Qur’anic passages.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r2.anchor: وقيل: المعنى واذكر إذ نادى كما صرح به في قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r3.claim: A further construal treats the phrase as introducing what happened when the Lord called Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r3.anchor: وقيل: المعنى { وإذ نادى ربك موسى } كان كذا وكذا

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r4.claim: Calling is addressing someone with the vocative “O so-and-so”; God said, “O Moses.”
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r4.anchor: والنداء الدعاء بيا فلان، أي قال ربك يا موسى

QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.claim: The command to approach the unjust people and the question about fearing God imply that they do not fear Him and that Moses was to call them to piety.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:10-13/r7.anchor: وقيل هذا من الإيماء إلى الشيء لأنه أمره أن يأتي القوم الظالمين، ودل قوله: { يتقون } على أنهم لا يتقون
